procedures.title: Straight-and-level flight
procedures.briefing: Basic cruise technique for Exercise 6: establish and maintain straight and level flight at cruise speed using an outside reference point.
steps: Look out - select an outside reference point
Pitch for horizontal flight
Speed 110 KIAS (approx. 65% power setting)
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Look out and check: fuel quantity and fuel balance, radio, engine instruments, direction (outside reference point), altitude
completion_standards: 110 KIAS at approx. 65% power setting
Wings level using ailerons, ball centered
Direction (outside reference point) and altitude maintained

procedures.title: Level-off from climb (110 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Used to level off at the target altitude after a climb and accelerate to cruise speed.
steps: Approx. 20 ft before target altitude, set pitch for horizontal flight
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Approaching 110 KIAS, approx. 65% power
Trim as required
completion_standards: Pitch for horizontal flight approx. 20 ft before target altitude
110 KIAS at approx. 65% power
Wings level, ball centered

procedures.title: Transition to climb (80 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Used in Exercise 7 to transition from cruise to a full-power climb at 80 KIAS.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Check engine instruments
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Approaching 80 KIAS, set full power (100%)
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Trim as required
Look out and check: pitch attitude, direction, wings level, airspeed
completion_standards: 80 KIAS climb attitude with full power (100%)
Ball centered, pitch attitude, direction and wings level maintained

procedures.title: Transition to cruise descent (110 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Standard descent technique for Exercise 8: a cruise descent at 110 KIAS and 500 ft/min.
steps: Reduce power to approx. 20% (standard descent 500 ft/min)
Pitch to maintain 110 KIAS
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Look out and check: pitch attitude, direction, wings level, airspeed
completion_standards: Approx. 20% power for a standard descent of 500 ft/min
110 KIAS maintained
Wings level, ball centered

procedures.title: Level-off from cruise descent
procedures.briefing: Used to level off at the target altitude from a cruise descent and return to cruise flight.
steps: Approx. 20 ft before the target altitude, increase power to approx. 65%
Pitch for horizontal flight
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Speed 110 KIAS (approx. 65% power)
completion_standards: Power increased to approx. 65% approx. 20 ft before the target altitude
110 KIAS at approx. 65% power
Wings level, ball centered

procedures.title: Transition to descent for approach (90 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Used to transition from cruise to a 90 KIAS descent for approach.
steps: Lookout - safety scan for traffic
Power - smoothly reduce power lever to approx. 20%
Attitude - maintain backpressure to decelerate to 90 KIAS, then set pitch attitude to capture descent
Trim - trim as required to maintain 90 KIAS
completion_standards: 90 KIAS maintained at approx. 20% power
Descent captured with pitch attitude

procedures.title: Level-off from descent for approach (90 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Used to level off at the target altitude from a descent for approach at 90 KIAS.
steps: Approx. 50 ft before target altitude, smoothly increase power to level flight setting (approx. 45%)
Attitude - pitch for horizontal flight (nose attitude is slightly higher than normal cruise)
Trim - trim as required to maintain 90 KIAS
completion_standards: Power smoothly increased to approx. 45% approx. 50 ft before target altitude
90 KIAS maintained; nose attitude slightly higher than normal cruise

procedures.title: Transition to glide descent (75 KIAS)
procedures.briefing: Used to transition to a power-off glide descent at 75 KIAS.
steps: Look out - select an outside reference point
Check engine instruments
Power idle
Set pitch for gliding flight (75 KIAS)
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Look out and check: pitch attitude, direction, wings level, airspeed
completion_standards: 75 KIAS gliding flight with power idle
Wings level, ball centered

procedures.title: Level-off from glide descent
procedures.briefing: Used to level off at the target altitude from a glide descent and accelerate back to cruise.
steps: Approx. 100 ft before the target altitude, increase power to increase speed to 110 KIAS (approx. 65% power)
Pitch for horizontal flight
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
completion_standards: Power increased approx. 100 ft before the target altitude
110 KIAS at approx. 65% power
Wings level, ball centered

procedures.title: Normal coordinated turn (30 degrees bank)
procedures.briefing: Basic turning technique for Exercise 9: a coordinated level turn at 30 degrees of bank.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Roll into 30 degrees bank, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Look out and check: bank / slip indicator, altitude / pitch
Roll out, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
completion_standards: 30 degrees of bank maintained
Coordinated flight (adverse yaw counteracted with rudder)
Altitude / pitch maintained

procedures.title: Climbing turn
procedures.briefing: Combines the Exercise 7 climb with a turn; bank is limited to a maximum of 20 degrees.
steps: Look out, check engine instruments
Establish normal climb (as explained in Exercise 7)
Max. bank 20 degrees, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Look out and check: bank / slip indicator, speed / pitch
Roll out, stay coordinated
Level-off (as explained in Exercise 7)
completion_standards: Maximum 20 degrees of bank
Coordinated flight throughout roll-in and roll-out
Normal climb (Exercise 7) and level-off maintained

procedures.title: Descending turn
procedures.briefing: Combines the Exercise 8 cruise descent with a turn at 30 degrees of bank.
steps: Look out
Establish cruise descent (as explained in Chapter 8, power approx. 25%)
Bank 30 degrees, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Look out and check: bank / slip indicator, speed / pitch
Look out, roll out, stay coordinated
Level-off or continue descent (as explained in Chapter 8)
completion_standards: 30 degrees of bank
Cruise descent at approx. 25% power
Coordinated flight throughout

procedures.title: Decelerate from 110 to 60 KIAS (flaps T/O)
procedures.briefing: Exercise 10A slow flight entry with flaps take-off: decelerate from cruise to 60 KIAS while maintaining altitude and direction.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Set power approx. 20%
Flaps T/O below 108 KIAS, adjust pitch
Maintain altitude / direction
Speed approaches 60 KIAS, set power approx. 35%
Trim
completion_standards: Flaps T/O selected below 108 KIAS
60 KIAS at approx. 35% power
Altitude and direction maintained

procedures.title: Accelerate from 60 to 110 KIAS (flaps T/O)
procedures.briefing: Recovery from slow flight with flaps take-off: accelerate back to cruise at 110 KIAS.
steps: Full power (100%)
Flaps up (speed approx. 70 KIAS), adjust pitch
Maintain altitude / direction
Approaching 110 KIAS, reduce power to approx. 65%
Readjust pitch and trim
Check horizontal flight
completion_standards: Full power (100%) for the acceleration
Flaps up at approx. 70 KIAS
110 KIAS at approx. 65% power, altitude and direction maintained

procedures.title: Decelerate from 110 to 65 KIAS (flaps up)
procedures.briefing: Exercise 10A slow flight entry in the clean configuration: decelerate from cruise to 65 KIAS while maintaining altitude and direction.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Set power approx. 20%
Readjust pitch and trim
Approaching 65 KIAS, power approx. 35%
Trim
Maintain altitude / direction
completion_standards: 65 KIAS at approx. 35% power, flaps up
Altitude and direction maintained

procedures.title: Accelerate from 65 to 110 KIAS (flaps up)
procedures.briefing: Recovery from clean slow flight: accelerate back to cruise at 110 KIAS.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Full power (100%)
Maintain altitude / direction / engine instruments
Approaching 110 KIAS, reduce power to approx. 65%
Readjust pitch and trim
Check horizontal flight
completion_standards: Full power (100%) for the acceleration
110 KIAS at approx. 65% power, flaps up
Altitude and direction maintained

procedures.title: Accelerate from 65 KIAS to max speed
procedures.briefing: Exercise 10A technique to accelerate from slow flight (65 KIAS) to maximum speed at full power.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Check engine instruments
Full power (100%)
Maintain altitude / direction
Adjust pitch and trim
completion_standards: Full power (100%)
Altitude and direction maintained
Pitch and trim adjusted for max speed

procedures.title: Pre-stall checklist
procedures.briefing: Inside and outside inspection performed before every stall, also before every approach to the stall.
steps: Inside inspection - Trim: checked (trimmed for level flight)
Inside inspection - Flaps: retracted (UP)
Inside inspection - Engine: checked (instruments in green, fuel balanced)
Inside inspection - Security: checked (harnesses tight, baggage stowed)
Outside inspection - Altitude: checked
Outside inspection - Position: checked
Outside inspection - Orientation: checked
Outside inspection - Sky: free
completion_standards: Recovered before: full stall 2000 ft AGL dual / 3000 ft AGL solo; approach to the stall 1500 ft AGL dual / 2500 ft AGL solo
Never stall above built up areas, harbours and industrial areas, populated areas, airports / CTRs, extended water areas, 4/8 clouds or more, or other traffic
Orientation: choose an outside reference point
Sky: make 90 degrees right and left clearing turns or a left hand 180 degrees turn to check the airspace ahead and below for other traffic

procedures.title: Full stall without flaps selected (clean)
procedures.briefing: Full stall entry in the clean configuration; preceded by the pre-stall checklist and a crew briefing covering type of stall, altitude to maintain and regain, and direction or heading to maintain.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Power idle
Maintain altitude, don't use the trim
Maintain coordinated flight
Move the stick progressively backwards until the stall
completion_standards: Full stall recognised by nose and/or wing drop or (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure
Recovery of the stall is started at nose and/or wing drop or (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure

procedures.title: Full stall recovery with power (clean)
procedures.briefing: Standard full stall recovery using power, returning to the original altitude in a climb.
steps: Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Check for increasing speed (approx. 70 KIAS)
Pitch up gently while moving the power lever gently forward to reach full power when the nose is passing through the horizon
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Climb back to original altitude
Speed 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)
completion_standards: Speed increasing (approx. 70 KIAS) before pitching up
Full power reached as the nose passes through the horizon
Climb attitude 80 KIAS, climb back to original altitude, then 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)

procedures.title: Full stall recovery without power (clean)
procedures.briefing: Full stall recovery without using power; the aircraft is established in a glide before climbing back to the original altitude.
steps: Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Check for increasing speed (approx. 70 KIAS)
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Adjust pitch for glide attitude (75 KIAS), trim
When established in the glide, end the exercise and climb back to original altitude
Speed 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)
completion_standards: Speed increasing (approx. 70 KIAS)
Glide attitude 75 KIAS established and trimmed
Climb back to original altitude, then 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)

procedures.title: Approach to stall in the landing configuration
procedures.briefing: Approach-to-stall entry in the landing configuration; recover at the first indication of the approaching stall.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Reduce to downwind speed, power approx. 20%
Approaching 90 KIAS, power approx. 45%
Check speed below 108 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" -> select flaps take-off
Power approx. 15%
Check speed below 91 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" -> select flaps landing
Maintain altitude (don't use the trim)
Wait for the first indication of approaching the stall
completion_standards: Flaps take-off below 108 KIAS, flaps landing below 91 KIAS
Recover at stall warning, 5 KIAS above the bottom white arc with flaps landing, or the buffet - whichever comes first

procedures.title: Approach to stall recovery in the landing configuration
procedures.briefing: Recovery from an approach to stall in the landing configuration with full power, climbing back to the previous altitude.
steps: Recover at the stall warning, buffet or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
Pitch down slightly to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Smoothly apply full power (100%)
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Pull up gently, pitch for climb attitude
Select flaps take-off
Speed > 70 KIAS, flaps up
Climb back to previous altitude
Speed 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)
completion_standards: Recovery at stall warning, buffet or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
Flaps up above 70 KIAS
Climb back to previous altitude, then 110 KIAS (approx. 65%)

procedures.title: Approach to stall in descending turn in approach configuration
procedures.briefing: Approach-to-stall entry in a descending turn in the approach configuration, simulating a base-to-final scenario.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Reduce to downwind speed, power approx. 20%
Approaching 90 KIAS, power approx. 45%
Check speed below 108 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" -> select flaps take-off
Power approx. 15%
Start descending turn with 20 degrees bank
Slowly raise the nose until airspeed bleeds off
Wait for the first indication of approaching the stall
completion_standards: Flaps take-off below 108 KIAS
Descending turn with 20 degrees of bank
Recover at stall warning, buffet or 5 knots above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first

procedures.title: Approach to stall recovery for descending turn in approach configuration
procedures.briefing: Recovery from an approach to stall in a descending turn: level the wings and apply full power.
steps: Recovery at the stall warning, buffet or 5 knots above the bottom of the white arc whichever comes first
Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Roll wings level
Smoothly apply full power (100%)
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Flaps up
Climb back to original altitude
completion_standards: Recovery at stall warning, buffet or 5 knots above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
Climb attitude 80 KIAS, climb back to original altitude

procedures.title: Approach to stall in climbing turn with flaps retracted
procedures.briefing: Approach-to-stall entry in a climbing turn in the clean configuration, simulating a departure scenario.
steps: Look out, PID or heading
Flaps up configuration
Start climbing turn with 15 degrees bank
Slowly raise the nose until airspeed bleeds off
Wait for a sign of the approaching stall
completion_standards: Climbing turn with 15 degrees of bank, flaps up
Recover at stall warning, 5 KIAS above the bottom of the green arc with flaps landing, or the buffet - whichever comes first

procedures.title: Approach to stall recovery for climbing turn with flaps retracted
procedures.briefing: Recovery from an approach to stall in a climbing turn: roll out of the turn and accelerate under full power.
steps: Recovery at the stall warning, buffet or 5 knots above the bottom of the green arc, whichever comes first
Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Roll out of the turn
Maintain full power, accelerate to 110 KIAS
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Climb or descent to desired altitude
completion_standards: Recovery at stall warning, buffet or 5 knots above the bottom of the green arc, whichever comes first
Full power maintained, accelerate to 110 KIAS
Return to desired altitude

procedures.title: Wing dip recovery
procedures.briefing: Exercise 11 recovery technique for a wing dip at the incipient spin; breaks the stall and stops the rotation.
steps: Power idle, ailerons neutral
Call "Recover" simultaneous pitch down below glide attitude to break the stall
Full opposite rudder with feet
Neutralize the rudder with feet when rotation stops
Check for increasing speed (approx. 80 KIAS)
Pull gently out of the dive, while moving the power lever gently forward, to reach full power when the nose is passing through the horizon
Direction with feet, no bank
Adjust pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Climb back to previous altitude
completion_standards: Rotation stopped with full opposite rudder
Speed increasing (approx. 80 KIAS)
Full power reached as the nose passes through the horizon
Climb attitude 80 KIAS, climb back to previous altitude

procedures.title: Emergency spin recovery
procedures.briefing: Just in case you don't know the procedure anymore; this general procedure is applicable for all JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided mass & balance falls in the envelope and the aircraft is trimmed for cruise flight. Consult the AFM/Diamond for the DA40 specific procedure.
steps: Power idle
Ailerons and elevator neutral
Apply full opposite rudder against rotation
Neutralize rudder
Pull gently out of the dive, wings level
Full power when nose is passing the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude
completion_standards: Rotation stopped, wings level
Full power when nose is passing the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude

procedures.title: Normal take-off
procedures.briefing: Standard Exercise 12 take-off and initial climb procedure for the DA40-TDI, including all line-up items and verbal calls.
steps: Confirm correct runway from signage / markings. Call out: "Runway [number], identified"
Scan the approach sector and the full length of the runway. Call out: "Approach sector and runway clear"
Line-up items: parking brakes released, transponder ALT, landing light on when clearance received, pitot heat ON (in visible moisture or if OAT is below +5 degrees C)
Line up on the runway centerline
Check runway direction. Call out: "Runway heading verified"
Check the windsock, ailerons into the wind
Heels on the floor, look down the end of the runway
Set full power (100%)
Maintain runway centreline using the rudder
Check CED - power 100% / 2300 RPM / all indications green. Call out: "Take-off power set"
Confirm the airspeed indicator is reading. Call out: "Airspeed alive"
Reduce ailerons input when accelerating / keep glare shield parallel to horizon
Rotate at 60 KIAS (Vr)
Pitch for climb speed 70 KIAS
Maintain runway track using ailerons
Maintain coordination using the rudder (ball centered)
Passing 200 ft AGL select flaps up
Set pitch for climb 80 KIAS
completion_standards: CED check: power 100% / 2300 RPM / all indications green
Rotate at 60 KIAS (Vr), pitch for climb speed 70 KIAS
Flaps up passing 200 ft AGL
Climb at 80 KIAS on runway track, ball centered

procedures.title: Crosswind take-off
procedures.briefing: Take-off in crosswind conditions: as a normal take-off with a slightly higher rotation speed and a coordinated turn into the wind once airborne.
steps: Proceed as normal take off (items 1-10)
Vr + max 5 KIAS during strong crosswind (1/2 gust)
Reduce ailerons input / keep glare shield parallel to horizon
Steer towards aiming point, use small rudder inputs
Once airborne make a coordinated turn into the wind
Maintain runway track using ailerons
Correct for increasing crosswind during the climb
Proceed as normal take off (items 13-19)
completion_standards: Rotate at Vr + max 5 KIAS during strong crosswind (1/2 gust)
Runway track maintained using ailerons
Coordinated turn into the wind once airborne

procedures.title: Short field take-off
procedures.briefing: Proceed as normal take-off, with the below changes: use all available runway length, full power against the brakes, and a lower rotation speed.
steps: Line up items before or when crossing the stop-bar
Line up at the very beginning of the runway (use all available length)
Hold the brakes, look down to the far end of the runway
Feet on the brakes
Check compass to identify runway direction
Check the windsock, ailerons in the wind
Full power (100%) 2300 rpm
Check power / engine instruments
Release brakes, heels on the floor
Direction with feet
Rotate at 55 KIAS (Vr)
Accelerate in ground effect once airborne
Start climb when speed > 59 KIAS
Proceed as normal take off (items 13-19)
completion_standards: Full power (100%) 2300 rpm set and checked against the brakes
Rotate at 55 KIAS (Vr)
Accelerate in ground effect; start climb when speed > 59 KIAS

procedures.title: Soft field take-off
procedures.briefing: Take-off from a soft surface (e.g. grass): a rolling take-off with back pressure on the stabilator to relieve the nose wheel.
steps: Proceed as normal take off (items 1-6)
Make a rolling take off (especially on long grass)
Gently full power 100%
Check power / engine instruments
Direction with feet
Maintain back pressure on the stabilator
Release back pressure when nose wheel lifts off
Proceed as short field take off (items 11-13)
completion_standards: Rolling take-off, gently full power 100%
Back pressure maintained until the nose wheel lifts off
Then as short field take-off: rotate at 55 KIAS (Vr), accelerate in ground effect, start climb when speed > 59 KIAS

procedures.title: Obstacle take-off
procedures.briefing: Short field take-off technique with a steep initial climb at 59 KIAS to clear an obstacle after take-off.
steps: Proceed as short field take off (items 1-11)
Initial climb 59 KIAS
Speed 80 KIAS after passing obstacle
Proceed as normal take off (items 13-19)
completion_standards: Initial climb at 59 KIAS until the obstacle is passed
Accelerate to 80 KIAS after passing the obstacle

procedures.title: Normal circuit and approach
procedures.briefing: Standard Exercise 13 circuit pattern flown at circuit altitude, ending on a stabilized final approach at 70 KIAS with flaps landing.
steps: Climb to circuit altitude and level off
Speed 90 KIAS, power approx. 45%
Look out and turn to crosswind, 30 degrees bank
Climbing turn after passing 200 ft is permitted to stay in the circuit area (climbing turn max 20 degrees bank)
Look out and turn to downwind, 30 degrees bank
Downwind checks (FRESBL)
Turn to base leg when runway is 45 degrees behind
Reduce power to approx. 15%
Maintain altitude until 80 KIAS, start descent
Trim as required, PID
Turn to final, maximum 30 degrees of bank
On final: flaps LDG, 70 KIAS, trimmed (adjust power as required to maintain glide path)
Establish on stabilized glide path
completion_standards: Circuit flown at 90 KIAS, approx. 45% power
Crosswind and downwind turns at 30 degrees bank (climbing turn max 20 degrees bank)
Base turn when runway is 45 degrees behind, power approx. 15%
Final: flaps LDG, 70 KIAS, trimmed, on a stabilized glide path

procedures.title: Downwind checks (FRESBL)
procedures.briefing: Memory items performed on the downwind leg of the circuit: Flaps, Radio, Engine, Security, Brakes, Lights.
steps: F - Flaps: check speed, call "SPEED CHECKED" -> select flaps take-off
R - Radio: downwind call (e.g., PH-RAB downwind runway 06)
E - Engine: instruments in green, fuel quantity & balance checked
S - Security: harnesses secure, loose items stowed
B - Brakes: check pressure, heels on floor
L - Lights: landing light ON
completion_standards: Speed checked before selecting flaps take-off
Engine instruments in green, fuel quantity & balance checked
Harnesses secure, brakes checked, landing light ON

procedures.title: Normal landing
procedures.briefing: Standard landing from a final approach at 70 KIAS with flaps landing, flaring to touchdown on the main wheels.
steps: Fly standard circuit
On final: flaps landing
70 KIAS final approach speed
Trim as required
Aim for the aiming point
Close the power lever gently
Start horizontal flight just before touchdown, and shift vision from the aiming point to the end of the runway or beyond using peripheral vision
Maintain directional control with rudder
Maintain runway centreline (lateral movement) using ailerons
Increase pitch attitude, maintain level flight (flare)
Touchdown on main wheels
Lower the nose gently
Elevator neutral / keep aileron in the wind
Decelerate by gently increasing brake pressure or as required
Vacate the runway when convenient
After passing the stop bar: perform the after landing checks (memory items)
completion_standards: 70 KIAS final approach speed with flaps landing
Touchdown on main wheels after a flare
After landing checks (memory items) performed after passing the stop bar

procedures.title: Crosswind landing
procedures.briefing: Landing in crosswind conditions: de-crab with rudder and bank into the wind to stay over the centreline at touchdown.
steps: Fly standard circuit and landing (item 1-6)
Correct for crosswind on all legs
Start horizontal flight just before touch down
Use rudder to de-crab and line up with the centreline, at the same time:
Bank into the wind to stay above the centreline
Maintain direction with feet (point in distance)
Smoothly close power lever and increase pitch attitude for the flare
Land the aircraft in this attitude while maintaining the nose at the aiming point and the ailerons in the wind to stay over the centreline
Proceed as normal landing (items 13-16)
completion_standards: De-crab with rudder lined up with the centreline while banking into the wind
Direction maintained with feet, ailerons in the wind
After landing checks (memory items) performed after passing the stop bar

procedures.title: Short field landing
procedures.briefing: Landing on a short field: a stabilized approach at 65 KIAS with the power closed in the tempo of the flare.
steps: Fly standard circuit
Landing configuration set at beginning of final
Establish on stabilized glide path
Power / attitude 65 KIAS, trim
Landing procedure as normal landing (item 7-14)
But, close power lever gently in the tempo of the flare
Ideally the power should just be closed as the aircraft touches down (not before touchdown!)
Proceed as normal landing (items 12-16)
completion_standards: 65 KIAS on a stabilized final, trimmed
Power closed in the tempo of the flare, just as the aircraft touches down (not before touchdown!)

procedures.title: Soft field landing (grass runway)
procedures.briefing: Landing on a soft/grass runway: keep the aircraft rolling with backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel.
steps: Fly standard circuit (items 1-13)
After touchdown and during taxi, maintain backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel pressure
Decelerate gently, but don't use excessive brakes
Keep aileron in the wind
Keep the aircraft rolling
Leave the runway when convenient
Perform the after landing checks while rolling
completion_standards: Backpressure on the elevator maintained after touchdown and during taxi
Gentle deceleration without excessive brakes
After landing checks performed while rolling

procedures.title: Touch and go
procedures.briefing: Landing followed immediately by a take-off: reconfigure to flaps take-off and apply full power on the runway centreline.
steps: Aim for the centreline
Set flaps take-off (visual check)
Full power 100% / 2300 RPM
Proceed as normal take off
completion_standards: Flaps take-off set (visual check)
Full power 100% / 2300 RPM
Proceed as normal take off

procedures.title: Go-around
procedures.briefing: Aborted approach: apply full power, arrest the descent and climb away in the take-off configuration.
steps: Call: "Going-around!"
Full power (100%)
Pitch up to arrest the descent (look outside)
Set flaps take-off
Pitch for climb attitude (70 KIAS)
Maintain coordinated flight
Reset trim
Proceed as normal take off (items 12-14)
completion_standards: Full power (100%) and descent arrested
Flaps take-off, climb attitude 70 KIAS
Coordinated flight, trim reset

procedures.title: Rejected take-off
procedures.briefing: Circuit emergency procedure to abort the take-off roll: close the power immediately, stop on the runway and vacate.
steps: Call out: "Aborting!"
Close the power immediately
Maintain runway centreline using rudder
Apply brakes as necessary
Elevator neutral / aileron into the wind
RT call: "call sign, rejected take-off"
Vacate the runway as soon as practical
completion_standards: Power closed immediately, runway centreline maintained
Brakes applied as necessary
Runway vacated as soon as practical

procedures.title: Simulated engine failure after take-off (SEFATO)
procedures.briefing: Circuit emergency procedure for an engine failure after take-off: pitch for the glide, select a landing area and land ahead.
steps: Pitch for glide attitude
Select a landing area
Avoid obstacles
Troubleshoot (time permitting)
Flaps T/O when landing assured
Adjust attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps)
Plan full flaps landing
Crash drill
Touchdown
For actual failure: evacuate the airplane and call RAC. (For training: go-around at minimum safe height)
completion_standards: Glide attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps)
Flaps T/O when landing assured, plan full flaps landing
For training: go-around at minimum safe height; for actual failure: evacuate the airplane and call RAC

procedures.title: Glide in (from circuit altitude)
procedures.briefing: Power-off approach from circuit altitude. Judge the power closed point based on wind direction and speed to reach the field safely; S-turns and side-slipping must only be used as a last resort to lose excess height, not as a primary method to correct the glide path.
steps: Fly standard circuit (items 1-6), but
No flaps on downwind, speed 90 KIAS
Maintain circuit altitude on downwind and/or base depending on wind direction and speed
Maintain speed 90 KIAS
Close power lever when landing is assured (estimate based on wind and conditions)
Glide speed 75 KIAS
Select flaps when landing assured
Adjust attitude to maintain 75 KIAS
Final checks
Plan full flaps landing, touch down at 60 KIAS
Proceed as normal landing (items 7-16)
completion_standards: 90 KIAS on downwind/base without flaps
Power closed when landing is assured, glide speed 75 KIAS
Full flaps landing, touch down at 60 KIAS

procedures.title: Flapless landing
procedures.briefing: Landing without flaps: higher approach speeds and a higher nose attitude, with no flare at touchdown.
steps: Fly standard circuit
Maintain 90 KIAS on downwind
Speed 85 KIAS on base leg
Establish on stabilized glide path
Power / attitude 75 KIAS on final
Nose attitude higher than for normal landing
Aim for the aiming point
Close power lever gently
Do not flare out, maintain a slightly higher attitude during touchdown
Proceed as normal landing (items 12-16)
completion_standards: 90 KIAS on downwind, 85 KIAS on base leg, 75 KIAS on final
No flare; slightly higher attitude maintained during touchdown

procedures.title: Wave-off
procedures.briefing: A wave-off is a go-around below 50 ft AGL, flown without turns at low altitude.
steps: Wave-off is a go-around below 50 ft AGL
Don't attempt to make turns at low altitude
Due to aircraft inertia, the main wheels may briefly touch the runway (do not pull back excessively to prevent this, and do not deliberately land)
Proceed as go-around
completion_standards: Go-around initiated below 50 ft AGL without turns at low altitude
No excessive pull-back if the main wheels briefly touch the runway; do not deliberately land
Proceed as go-around

procedures.title: Steep turn (45 degrees bank)
procedures.briefing: Exercise 15 advanced turning: a coordinated turn at 45 degrees of bank with added power to maintain 110 KIAS.
steps: Look out - scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Speed 110 KIAS
Roll into 45 degrees bank, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Passing 30 degrees bank, increase power by approx. 10%
Look out and check: bank / slip indicator, altitude / pitch, maintain 110 KIAS
Roll out, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw
When passing 30 degrees of bank, reduce power by approx. 10%
Adjust pitch for horizontal flight
completion_standards: 45 degrees of bank, coordinated (rudder against adverse yaw)
Power increased approx. 10% passing 30 degrees bank and reduced approx. 10% when rolling out through 30 degrees of bank
110 KIAS and altitude maintained

procedures.title: Spiral dive recovery
procedures.briefing: Recovery from a spiral dive (the spiral dive entry is flown with FI only: steep turn with 45 degrees of bank, nose lowered gently below the horizon, noticing increase of speed and G force).
steps: Reduce the power
Roll out gently, wings level
Pitch up gently to climb attitude
Full power when nose passes the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude
completion_standards: Power reduced, wings level before pitching up
Full power when nose passes the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude

procedures.title: Forced landing procedure
procedures.briefing: Exercise 16 procedure for an engine failure in flight: glide at 75 KIAS, select a field, troubleshoot, and fly a pattern via the 1000 ft point to a full flaps landing.
steps: Maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS and start looking for a suitable field
Pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS
Depending on altitude/position turn downwind and select a landing area, below 1200 ft turn direct base leg for the most suitable landing area
Perform abbreviated troubleshoot
Select the most suitable landing area within reach and use to the 1000 ft point
May Day call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T) (when time permitting)
Proceed to the 1000 ft point
Perform expanded trouble shoot if possible, perform the restart procedure
After passing the 1000 ft point turn to base leg
On final aim at 1/3 of the field to guarantee making the field
Flaps T/O when landing assured
Adjust attitude for 70 KIAS
Plan full flaps landing 60 KIAS
When landing is assured, shift aiming point to the beginning of runway or field
Perform crash drill (memory items)
Avoid obstacles
Evacuate the airplane and call RAC
completion_standards: Glide attitude trimmed for 75 KIAS
Below 1200 ft turn direct base leg for the most suitable landing area
May Day call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T) when time permitting
On final aim at 1/3 of the field; flaps T/O when landing assured, 70 KIAS
Full flaps landing 60 KIAS

procedures.title: Crash drills
procedures.briefing: Memory items performed before touchdown in a forced landing to secure the aircraft. (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY!!!
steps: Seat belts - fastened
Fuel selector - closed (T)
Flaps - set
Electric Master - off (T)
completion_standards: (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY!!! items are only touched, not actuated, in training
After landing: evacuate the airplane and call RAC

procedures.title: Precautionary landing procedure
procedures.briefing: Consider a precautionary landing when weather deteriorates below VMC minima, after UDP, or other circumstance affecting flight safety that require a precautionary landing; the aircraft should be technically in a good condition. The field is inspected from the air before landing.
steps: Perform downwind checks and select flaps T/O
Fly down the wind
PAN PAN call / transponder on 7700 / ELT man (T)
Position on downwind of the suitable field
Fly a close circuit at 500 ft AGL
Be aware of high obstacles
Make a descending turn towards the selected area and carry out an inspection run at 200 ft AGL; check the condition of the landing area
Check the compass direction in poor visibility
Aim for a landmark in good visibility
Climb to 500 ft AGL, flaps up on the up-wind leg
Turn to crosswind
Check the location of the landing area
Continue the turn to downwind, downwind checks
Turn to final when the landing area is 60 degrees behind the wing
Carry out a short field landing
Evacuate the airplane and call RAC
completion_standards: Close circuit at 500 ft AGL, inspection run at 200 ft AGL
Turn to final when the landing area is 60 degrees behind the wing
Short field landing carried out
Landing field requirements: no obstacles on final (or upwind), long enough (min. 300 m), headwind (or light crosswind), flat, preference for (short) grassland over plowed land
